questions.title: How does the implicit reward function in DPO avoid the need for explicit reward modeling?
questions.question_body: In the DPO derivation, we replace the reward function $r(x,y)$ with the form $r(x,y)= eta igl(	ext{log} rac{ oldsymbol{	heta}(y|x)}{	ext{ref}(y|x)} + 	ext{log}Z(x) igr)$.  Since $Z(x)$ is unknown, how do we guarantee that maximizing the DPO loss is equivalent to maximizing the original RLHF objective?  Does this mean that DPO implicitly learns a reward model that can be recovered from the policy, and if so how is that recovery performed?

questions.title: Why does the partition function $Z(x)$ cancel out when converting from a reward‑based Bradley‑Terry model to a policy‑based preference model?
questions.question_body: Equation (7) in the paper shows that after substituting $r(x,y)$ with its reparameterization, the $	ext{log} igl(Z(x) igr)$ term drops out of the preference probability.  Can someone walk through a step‑by‑step algebraic proof that demonstrates this cancellation explicitly?

questions.title: What exactly is being optimized when we minimize $	ext{L}_{	ext{DPO}}$?  Is it a softmax over all possible completions?
questions.question_body: The DPO loss (Eq. 8) involves $ eta	ext{log} rac{	heta(y|x)}{	ext{ref}(y|x)}$ inside a logistic function.  In language generation there are astronomically many possible completions $y$.  How does this loss still correspond to an expectation over all completions?  Does it implicitly only depend on the two completions present in each preference pair?

questions.title: How does DPO’s weighting term $ eta$ compare to PPO’s KL coefficient
questions.question_body: The gradient of DPO contains a factor $ eta igl(	ext{log} rac{	heta(y_w|x)}{	ext{ref}(y_w|x)}-	ext{log} rac{	heta(y_l|x)}{	ext{ref}(y_l|x)} igr)$ as a weight for each pair.  In PPO this weight emerges from the clipping or penalty on the KL divergence.  Are these two hyperparameters directly comparable?  How should I choose $ eta$ if I already have a PPO baseline with a particular target KL?

questions.title: Why can any reward class consistent with Bradley‑Terry be represented by the reparameterisation in Theorem 1?
questions.question_body: Theorem 1 claims that any reward function up to an additive function of $x$ can be written as $r(x,y)= eta	ext{log} rac{	heta(y|x)}{	ext{ref}(y|x)}$ for some policy $	heta$.  The proof in Appendix C introduces an operator $f(r;	ext{ref}, eta)$ that normalises rewards with $	ext{log}$ of a partition function.  Could someone give an intuitive example (e.g. a toy two‑token vocabulary) showing how this operator moves an arbitrary reward into that specific form while preserving preferences?

questions.title: What guarantees does DPO provide against over‑optimization or mode collapse?
questions.question_body: "Implicitly avoid baseline or value–function issues" is mentioned when comparing DPO to actor–critic methods.  However, is there any theoretical or empirical evidence that DPO can still suffer from mode collapse (i.e., generating only one high‑reward completion) if $ eta$ is set too low or if the preference data are sparse?

questions.title: How does DPO handle high‑dimensional outputs where computing $	heta(y|x)$ directly is infeasible?
questions.question_body: In practice, $	heta(y|x)$ is computed via autoregressive decoding where we multiply token probabilities sequentially.  The DPO loss uses $	heta(y|x)$ as a whole.  Does this imply we need to compute the full joint probability for each pair during training?  If so, what tricks (e.g., caching, log‐sum‐exp tricks) are used to make it tractable?

questions.title: "$ oldsymbol{	heta}$” vs "policy”: Are they literally identical and learnable via standard LM training?
questions.question_body: "Your Language Model Is Secretly a Reward Model" suggests that once we embed the LM in the DPO loss, it acts both as policy and reward model.  Does this mean I can take any pre‑trained transformer and fine‑tune it with cross‑entropy on labelled pairs, without treating it separately as policy?  How do we preserve parameters like logits or temperature during this joint optimisation?
